x: The Western Ghats give heavy orographic rain on the west coast, the funnel-shaped Meghalaya hills give Mawsynram the world's highest rainfall, the Himalayas confine the monsoon and the Aravallis give little rain as winds run parallel, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Relate each relief feature to its rainfall.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Western Ghats
(b) Meghalaya Hills
(c) Himalayas
(d) Aravallis

List-II
(i) Little orographic rainfall in Rajasthan because winds run roughly parallel
(ii) Orographic barrier that helps confine the monsoon
(iii) Heavy orographic rainfall on the windward west coast
(iv) Funnel-shaped hills giving the world's highest rainfall at Mawsynram

x: Both are true and R explains A: Arabian Sea winds strike the Western Ghats and rise, dropping heavy orographic rain on the west coast.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Tamil Nadu coast gets winter rain from the north-east monsoon, not Western Disturbances. J&K, Punjab and Haryana do get WD rain.

x: I, II and III are correct: Kerala and Mawsynram are very wet and the Thar very dry. IV is false because the rain-shadow Deccan receives low rainfall.
t: Check for a reversed rainfall claim.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Kerala is a key region of the heaviest rainfall along the Western Coast.
II. Mawsynram is a famous location associated with very heavy rainfall in Meghalaya.
III. Western Rajasthan and the Thar region receive very scanty rainfall.
IV. The rain-shadow Deccan receives very heavy rainfall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: Telangana is a rain-shadow area, and the interior Deccan is dry because it lies behind the Western Ghats.
All three are correct: the west coast and north-east are very wet, the Western Ghats and Meghalaya wet, and most northern plains and central India moderate.
Both are true and R explains A: Bay of Bengal winds forced up the funnel-shaped Meghalaya hills drop very heavy rain.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All five are rain-shadow areas: interior Maharashtra, interior Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
t: Recall the rain-shadow areas of India.

x: Both are true: Bay of Bengal winds bring Meghalaya its rain, and orographic uplift causes the extreme rain at Mawsynram.

Coastal Karnataka is a heavy-rain region of the west coast, the Thar of western Rajasthan is a very scanty rainfall zone, and the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills get very heavy rain in Meghalaya, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
